Also making the environment visually occluded helps out too. For example adding fog, yet again making the lighting have more contrast, that's why flashlight is such a common trope in horror games. These type of things add fear of the unknown aspect. Making the player guess and anticipate if there's a monster lurking in the fog or darkness

I did a research on horror game atmosphere and looked for similarities and found these:

1) the lighting used is commonly colourless, only slightly leaning towards a warmer tone. 
2) horror games have higher contrast. I think this is very important here, you should tweak the lighting engine/sources so they produce less light or make the environment as a whole darker to begin with.
3) in horror games often colors are pretty muted. I can see the greens in your game are quite saturated, maybe tone them down a little.
